cards.name: Ground friction, acceleration and run speed
cards.summary: The player runs at 250 units per second. Ground friction removes speed in proportion to a stop-speed floor, and ground acceleration is ten times stronger than air acceleration.
cards.behavior: Every movement step applies friction first, then acceleration. Friction only acts when the player walks on a non-slick floor and is not in a knockback state. The speed drop equals the larger of current speed and the stop speed, times the friction value, times the step time in seconds. Speeds below 1 unit per second snap to zero. Acceleration builds a wish direction from the input. The input is scaled so the largest axis maps to the full run speed, with 127 as the full analog value. Acceleration only adds the shortfall between current speed along the wish direction and the wish speed, so cruising at the cap adds nothing. In the air the same function runs with an acceleration of 1, so mid-air steering is weak and momentum carries. Crouching or rolling halves the wish speed. A movement step uses the time since the last command, clamped between 1 and 200 milliseconds. The server snaps command times to a multiple of the pmove step, which defaults to 8 milliseconds.

constants.name: friction coefficient
constants.unit: per second, multiplied by step time in seconds

constants.name: ground acceleration
constants.unit: per second, multiplied by step time in seconds

constants.name: air acceleration
constants.unit: per second, multiplied by step time in seconds

capabilities: speed-proportional braking with a stop floor

cards.name: Run speed multipliers by state
cards.summary: Base speed is rescaled each step by the current state: backward run, grip, force speed, rage and rage recovery.
cards.behavior: Each step the speed value resets to the server base speed, then state multipliers apply. Running backward on the ground without the walk button multiplies speed by 0.75. A player who is holding a force grip moves at 0.4 of base speed. Active force speed multiplies by 1.7. Active force rage multiplies by 1.3. After rage ends, a recovery period multiplies by 0.75. Force speed and rage do not stack, because the rage branch only runs when force speed is off. Dragging a body multiplies the server base speed by 0.2. A dodge or a knockdown sets speed to zero for its duration. The code also holds a table of force speed levels, but nothing reads it. So the 1.7 value is the same at every speed level, and the level only changes how long the power lasts.

constants.name: grip holder speed multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on speed while force gripping

constants.name: force speed multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on speed while force speed is active

constants.name: rage multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on speed while rage is active

constants.name: rage recovery multiplier
constants.unit: multiplier on speed during rage recovery

cards.name: Base jump, gravity and player hull
cards.summary: A plain jump launches at 225 units per second under 800 units per second squared gravity, which peaks near 32 units. The standing hull is 30 wide and 64 tall.
cards.behavior: A normal jump sets vertical velocity to a fixed launch speed and records the jump start height. The server sets gravity from a cvar each frame, and each movement step subtracts gravity times step time from vertical velocity. With these numbers a plain jump rises about 32 units, which matches the first force jump height tier. The player hull is 15 units on each side horizontally, so 30 wide, and spans from 24 below to 40 above the origin when standing. That is 64 tall. Crouching lowers the top to 16 above the origin. Steps up to 18 units are climbed automatically, and a slope counts as walkable when its surface normal Z is at least 0.7. A landing sets a short recovery timer of 130 milliseconds. While wall running, gravity is halved for as long as the run animation has more than 500 milliseconds left.

constants.name: hull half-extent on X and Y
constants.unit: units from origin to each side, so 30 wide

constants.name: wall run slow fall minimum remaining animation time

cards.name: Held force jump with four height tiers
cards.summary: Holding jump past the base height keeps adding upward speed until a tier cap of 32, 96, 192 or 384 units above the launch point. The force point drain scales with upward speed and divides by the tier.
cards.behavior: Force jump is a hold-to-rise jump. While jump stays held in the air and force points remain, the vertical speed each step comes from how far the player has climbed. The speed is the tier launch strength times the remaining fraction of the tier height, divided by 10, plus the base jump speed. So the lift fades smoothly as the cap nears. Climbing continues until the cap is reached, or until the player lets go after the base height, or until force points run out. Past the cap, upward speed is clamped to the base jump speed. The tier follows the levitation level, from 0 for a plain jump to 3 for the top tier. While the force jump is active, the game drains force points on a timer of 300 milliseconds at level 2 and above and 200 at level 1. The amount passed to the drain call is ignored. The drain function instead picks a cost from the current upward speed, 20 above 250 units per second, 16 above 200, 12 above 150, 8 above 100, and less below that. It then divides by the tier. Landing at or above the launch height caps the fall impact at a small value.

constants.name: lift fade divisor
constants.unit: dimensionless divisor on the scaled tier speed

constants.name: drain interval at level 2 and above
drain per event above 250 upward speed
constants.unit: force points per drain event before dividing by tier

constants.name: upward speed threshold for the largest drain
landing impact cap when landing at or above launch height

capabilities: force point cost scaled by rise speed

cards.name: Wall run, wall flip and backflip from the ground
cards.summary: Pressing jump while strafing near a wall launches a wall run or a wall flip. Pressing jump while moving back launches a backflip.
cards.behavior: These moves need a saber or melee weapon in hand. Wall run and wall flip need force jump level 2 or higher. The backflip needs level 1. On the ground, jump plus strafe plus forward picks a wall run. Jump plus strafe with no forward input picks a wall flip. Jump plus backward, with attack not held, picks a backflip that needs no wall. A short probe 16 units to the side checks for a wall. A wall run only starts when the wall is nearly vertical, with a surface normal Z between 0 and 0.4. The wall flip and the backflip kick the player 150 units per second away from the wall or backward and clear the old horizontal speed. Each move sets vertical speed from the level 2 launch strength divided by 2 for a run and 2.25 for a flip, plus 128 extra. The backflip uses the base jump speed plus 128. During a wall run the player floats with halved gravity. After the first 400 milliseconds and before the last 400 milliseconds of the run animation, pressing jump flips off the wall. The flip halves horizontal speed and kicks 150 units per second away.

constants.name: extra vertical shove
constants.unit: units per second added to the vertical push

constants.name: side kick speed for wall flip
maximum wall normal Z for a wall run
flip off wall horizontal speed scale
flip off wall edge guard
constants.unit: milliseconds at start and end of the run animation

capabilities: wall run along a vertical wall

cards.name: Air wall rebound and run-up-wall flip
cards.summary: At force jump level 3 the player can bounce off walls in mid-air at 200 units per second, and run up a wall for a flip.
cards.behavior: Two air moves reward the top jump level. In the air at level 3, pressing a direction toward a nearly vertical wall within 8 units rebounds off it. The player is pushed away at 200 units per second with an upward speed of the top launch strength divided by 2.5. Control stays off for half a second. The call passes a cost of 10 force points, but the drain function ignores it and uses the upward-speed rule, so the real cost at level 3 is 20 divided by 3, which is 6 points. Rebounds chain only while the climb since the jump start stays under the top height minus half the rebound strength, so the count of bounces is limited. The wall must have a surface normal Z of at most 0.2. The second move needs level 2 or higher, forward input and ground within 80 units while in a plain jump or in-air animation. The player probes 32 units ahead. On a wall, horizontal speed drops to zero and an upward kick applies. Level 3 uses half the top launch strength. Level 2 uses 150 up and 150 back. At level 3 the flip animation later ends with a 300 units per second push backward and 200 up.

constants.name: rebound push speed
constants.unit: units per second away from wall

constants.name: maximum wall normal Z for rebound
maximum ground distance to start run-up
level 3 run-up end backward push
constants.unit: units per second along the forward direction, so backward

capabilities: chained wall bounces in the air
run up a wall and flip

cards.name: Force point pool and regeneration
cards.summary: The pool holds 100 points and refills one point every 200 milliseconds, but only while no force power is active and the saber is not busy.
cards.behavior: Force points are a single pool with a maximum of 100. Regeneration runs on a timer in the server power update. The default delay comes from a cvar and is 200 milliseconds, which means 5 points per second. A source comment says half a second, but the cvar value is the effective one. Regeneration only runs when no force power is active, or only drain is active, and the thrown saber is not in flight, and the saber is not in a special move. A force boon powerup regenerates 6 points per step, and the Jedi Master game mode regenerates 4. The holocron mode adds one point per held holocron. In the Siege mode, an objective carrier regenerates one point per 7 seconds. In power duel, the lone duelist uses a shorter delay, 0.7 of the base with no frag limit, or 0.6 plus 0.3 times wins over the frag limit otherwise. Some powers need a minimum pool before they start, such as lightning and drain at 25 points.

constants.name: lone power duelist delay scale with no frag limit

capabilities: resource pool that refills only when idle

cards.name: Force power cost table by level
cards.summary: Each power has a force point cost per level. Push and pull cost 20 at every level, speed and rage 50, and protect and absorb fall from 50 to 10 as they level.
cards.behavior: A table indexed by level and power gives the amount that the pool must hold to use a power, and the amount taken for most powers. Level 0 lists 999, so nothing is usable without training. Heal costs 65, 60 and 50 at levels 1 to 3. Push, pull, mind trick, drain and force sight cost 20 at every level. Speed and rage cost 50 at every level. Protect and absorb cost 50, 25 and 10 by level. Team heal and team force cost 50, 33 and 25. Lightning lists 1, the amount taken per tick while held. Grip lists 30, 30 and 60. For grip the table only gates the start, since a fixed 30 points is taken on start and 1 point per 100 milliseconds after that. Saber throw lists 20, but no code path in this repository takes it. The table is the main balance lever for a force-based game.

cards.name: Force speed burst
cards.summary: Force speed costs 50 points, lasts 10, 15 or 20 seconds by level, and multiplies run speed by 1.7. A second press cancels it after a 1.5 second lock.
cards.behavior: Pressing the speed key toggles the power. The first press checks usability and the pool, then starts the power with a duration set by level. Level 1 lasts 10 seconds, level 2 lasts 15 seconds and level 3 lasts 20 seconds. The player cannot cancel it for 1.5 seconds. After that a second press ends it early. The movement code multiplies speed by 1.7 while the power is active. The key must be released before it can toggle again. While force speed is active the force pool does not regenerate, because regeneration only runs with no active power. A siege objective carrier that disables force cannot use it. The cost table lists 50 at all three levels.

cards.name: Force push and pull
cards.summary: Push and pull fling targets away or toward the player at 256 units per second per level minus 0.7 per unit of distance, within 1024 units.
cards.behavior: Both powers share one routine. The power fails while the player has weapon time left or is in a hand-extend animation. Level 1 is a single targeted ray of 512 units, so only the thing under the crosshair is affected. Levels 2 and 3 search everything within 1024 units and keep targets inside a view arc, with a parameter of 60 for level 2 and 180 for level 3, and in line of sight. Each affected player gets a velocity along the push direction. Its speed is 256 times the effective level minus 0.7 per unit of distance, with a floor of 16. A target with no vertical speed gets at least 128 units per second of upward kick. A target who is idle and has the same power at a level equal to or above the pusher level, or one less while moving, auto-counters and gets no push. A lower level only reduces it, by 20, 40 or 80 percent as the gap shrinks from 3 or more to 1. Level 3 push can also knock a close target down. Pull has a chance of 30, 70 or 100 percent by level, within 256 units, to yank a weapon from an enemy. Push also reflects incoming projectiles and triggers force-usable doors and props. Using push in a saber lock adds lock progress. The hand animation holds the player for 1000 milliseconds on push and 400 on pull.

constants.unit: divisor on the 1024 unit radius, so the ray is 512 units

constants.unit: units per second lost per unit of distance

cards.name: Force grip choke and lift
cards.summary: Grip reaches 256 units, takes 30 points to start and 1 point every 100 milliseconds, and deals 2 damage each second plus a burst at 3 seconds.
cards.behavior: Grip needs a clear ray to a target within 256 units. It takes a fixed 30 points on start, then 1 point every 100 milliseconds, which is 10 points per second, and ends if the pool empties. The victim takes 2 damage each second while held. At level 1 the victim stays on the ground and the grip lasts at most 5 seconds. At level 2 the victim floats up at 30 units per second and takes a 20 damage burst at 3 seconds, and the grip ends at 4 seconds. At level 3 the victim is pulled to a point 128 units in front of the gripper with a speed that grows with the gap, from 8 up to 700 units per second, updated every 300 milliseconds. The level 3 burst is 40 damage and the grip ends at 4 seconds. Below level 3 the victim must stay in front of the gripper. The gripper moves at 0.4 of normal speed. A push by the victim breaks the grip when its level matches or exceeds the grip level.

constants.name: start charge
constants.unit: force points taken once at start

constants.name: level 3 hold point distance in front

capabilities: damage over time with a burst

cards.name: Force lightning stream
cards.summary: Lightning needs 25 points to start, takes 1 point and does 1 to 2 damage every 50 milliseconds, and arcs to everything within 300 units at level 3.
cards.behavior: Lightning starts only with at least 25 points and no hand animation or weapon time active. It begins with 500 milliseconds of duration. At level 2 and above, holding the key extends the duration by another 500 milliseconds each step, so it runs while held. At level 1 it runs in short bursts. While active, a tick every 50 milliseconds fires the stream and takes 1 point, which is 20 points per second. Each tick does 1 or 2 damage to a target that can be hurt. A target with force absorb can turn the stream into a feed. In that case the stream does at most 1 damage, or none at the lowest effective level, and a short window follows in which the target gains force points instead. At level 3 the stream becomes an arc that checks every target within 300 units. Melee users at level 3 deal doubled damage. When lightning ends, the player cannot start it again for 1.5 seconds at level 2 and above, or 3 seconds at level 1. Hit players are electrified for 800 milliseconds and lose cloak.

constants.unit: force points per tick, from the level cost table

constants.unit: milliseconds added each step while held at level 2 and above

cards.name: Force rage and protect defensive buffs
cards.summary: Rage lasts 8 to 20 seconds, divides damage by level plus 1, and drains health. Protect lasts 20 seconds and absorbs 40, 60 or 80 percent of damage for force points.
cards.behavior: Rage and protect are mutually exclusive, along with absorb, and turning one on turns the others off. Both lock out cancel for 1.5 seconds after activation. Rage lasts 8, 14 or 20 seconds by level. While raging, damage from other characters divides by the level plus one, and speed rises by 30 percent. Rage drains 2 health on a timer of 150, 300 or 450 milliseconds by level, but never kills. It needs at least 10 health to start. When rage ends, a 10 second recovery period applies with reduced speed and weaker saber lock pushes. Protect lasts 20 seconds. While active, each hit has a part removed. Damage up to a cap is cut by 40, 60 or 80 percent by level. The cap is 100, 200 or 400 damage. Damage above the cap is removed in full. The force point price is 1, 0.5 or 0.25 per damage point inside the cap. When the pool cannot pay, the reduction shrinks.

constants.unit: damage points counted at the fraction

constants.name: protect force price per damage at level 3

cards.name: Saber swing damage from stance power and trace length
cards.summary: A swing hurts by 2.5 times the stance power level, doubled outside duel and siege, times trace length scaled by 0.033, and 1.5 times more against players.
cards.behavior: The default damage mode follows the single player rules, because the mode cvar defaults to 1. Each swing looks up a power level from the attack animation, 1 for fast, 2 for medium, dual and staff, and 3 for strong. A thrown saber uses 2.5 times the throw level on the way out, and a base factor of 1 on the way back. Base damage is 2.5 times the power level. Modes other than duel, power duel and siege double it. The final hit is that value times the length of the swept saber trace times 0.1 times 0.33, rounded up. A hit that starts earlier in the trace does more damage. A hit on a player multiplies by 1.5. A global cvar scales damage, and a broken arm cuts it to 30 percent. A blade resting on a target with no swing does 1 damage on a 350 millisecond cooldown.

cards.name: Saber attack power for parry breaks
cards.summary: Stance sets a base power from 1 to 3. An attacker doubles it and adds 1, then gains points from swing travel, with a bigger step for faster stances.
cards.behavior: Parries, knockaways and broken parries compare a power number, not the damage. The base is the stance level, where fast is 1, medium is 2, strong is 3, and dual and staff count as 2. When the player is attacking, the base doubles and gains 1. If the blade was sampled within 50 milliseconds of the last check, the distance the blade base traveled adds points. One point is added for each step of travel. The step is 8 units for strong, 16 for medium, dual and staff, and 24 for fast. So a fast swing needs more motion for the same bonus. A broken arm multiplies the value by 0.3. The result is then held to a sane range.

constants.unit: units of blade travel per bonus point

cards.name: Saber lock and mash-to-win resolution
cards.summary: Two blades that clash can lock for up to 10 seconds at 46 units apart. Each attack tap adds lock hits by stance, and a normal win with leftover hits knocks the loser down.
cards.behavior: A lock can start when a blocked or clashing swing happens. Both fighters must be on the ground, within 16 units in height, between 8 and 80 units apart, not crouching, not rolling, and have their sabers in hand. Between two human players the lock also needs a duel between those two, or a duel game mode. The chance is low. A clash roll of 20 sides passes with a lock factor of 2, so about 10 percent. A block of a hit passes about 5 percent, and 30 percent when the blocker has a saber offense level more than 1 above the attacker. The pair snaps to a spacing of 46 units for the newer lock animations. During the lock, each new press of attack adds lock hits by stance. Fast adds 1, medium, dual and staff add 2, and strong adds 3. A raging player adds 1 plus the rage level. Each press also adds a random 0 to 2. Each update with stored hits uses one hit and moves the lock animation by the offense level plus 1 frames. Whoever finishes the animation wins. A win is a super break when strength plus leftover hits beats a random 2 to 4. A super break plays a finishing animation. A normal win with leftover hits knocks the loser down for 1.1 seconds with a push of 8 times 40 units per second. If time runs out, or the pair drifts out of range, no one wins and both are shoved apart at 160 units per second.

cards.name: Thrown saber flight and recall
cards.summary: A thrown saber leaves at 400 units per second, reaches 700 units per throw level, and returns at 700 units per second, or 900 at level 3.
cards.behavior: Saber throw sends the blade as a projectile along the view direction at 400 units per second. The farthest it flies is 700 units times the throw level, and then it turns back. At level 2 and above the blade follows the view direction at 500 units per second, with a retarget about every 400 milliseconds. At level 3 the retarget interval is 100 milliseconds and the trace can aim at players. The return speed is 700 units per second, or 900 at level 3, and the speed drops by 100, 150 or 200 as the blade comes within 256, 128 or 64 units of the hand. A new throw has a 500 millisecond delay. Damage uses the single player swing formula with 2.5 times the throw level on the way out. While the saber flies, the thrower can still use force powers by default, and force points do not regenerate.

constants.name: slowdown near the hand within 256 units
constants.unit: units per second added to the return speed

constants.name: outbound damage factor per throw level

cards.name: Fall damage and landing roll
cards.summary: Landing impact is the square of the vertical speed times 0.0001. Damage starts above 44 and costs 0.16 per point. A crouched landing rolls and cuts the impact to a third.
cards.behavior: On landing, the game turns vertical speed into an impact number by squaring it and multiplying by 0.0001. Landing while crouched doubles the number. Shallow water scales it by 0.5 and chest-deep water by 0.25, and full submersion removes it. A crouched landing that can roll divides the impact by 3. The impact is sent as an event. The server ignores impacts of 44 or less. Above that, damage is the impact times 0.16, which bypasses armor. A knockdown state counts impacts above 14 at full value. After a force jump that started higher than the landing point, the impact is reduced by 0.3 times the unused force jump height of the tier, but never below 8. Landing at or above the launch point caps the event at 8. A roll also starts when a runner with a saber or melee weapon presses crouch at 200 units per second or more, and it needs 64 units of clear space in the roll direction.

constants.name: impact scale
constants.unit: factor on vertical speed squared, speed in units per second

constants.name: roll start speed squared
constants.unit: units squared per second squared, equals 200 units per second

cards.name: Optional limb removal on saber hits
cards.summary: Dismemberment is off by default. A cvar sets the percent chance, and a cut needs at least 5 damage.
cards.behavior: The limb removal check runs on a kill hit and on hits to a dead body, but the cvar that enables it defaults to 0, so nothing is cut unless the host turns it on. When enabled, the cvar value is the percent chance rolled against a random 0 to 100. The hit also needs at least 5 damage. At a cvar value of exactly 100, the hit location code also requires the hit direction and the blade direction to be roughly perpendicular to the limb cap. The dot product must stay within 0.5, or within 0.25 for waist and head, and the hit must land within 16 units of the cap. Only humanoid models and one droid class can lose limbs.

constants.name: perpendicular dot limit for waist and head

cards.name: Damped third-person chase camera
cards.summary: The chase camera sits 80 units behind a point 16 units above the view point, eases toward it, and uses an 8 unit box to avoid walls. Third person is off by default.
cards.behavior: The camera first finds a target point at the view point plus a vertical offset. The camera then sits behind the target along the view direction by a range cvar. A box of 4 units half-extent, so 8 units wide, traces from the player to the target and from the target to the camera, and the camera stops at any hit. Pitch is clamped to 89 degrees. Both points ease toward their ideal place with an exponential decay that runs per 50 millisecond step. The target eases with a factor of 0.5. The camera eases with a base factor of 0.3. The factor grows with the square of pitch over 115 in either direction, so the camera is stiffer when pitched far. Fast yaw turns add a stiffness bonus. Teleports and vehicles skip the damping. The default field of view is 80 degrees. Third person itself defaults to off and a cvar toggles it.

constants.name: collision box half-extent
constants.unit: units per axis, so 8 units wide

constants.name: target damping
constants.unit: fraction of the gap closed per 50 millisecond step

constants.name: camera damping base
constants.unit: fraction of the gap closed per 50 millisecond step
